messages.content: I am adding a Logger to today's challenge. I need the team's destination and source-location convention, not a generic spdlog sample.
I want to add a simple logging facility to a C++ program. Which destinations should it support, and what source location should each line show?
Logging supports file and stdout, stdout is the default, records use __FILE__ and __LINE__, and display only the filename.

The holiday page is HTML, not JSON. I need the HTTP and parse libraries this repo already standardized on, including that both must be linked.
Which libraries should a C++ scrape of officeholidays.com use, and must both be linked?
Web scraping uses libcurl for HTTP and libxml2 for HTML parsing; both libraries must be checked and linked.
Which libraries should a C++ scrape of officeholidays.com use, and must both be linked?
The Logger constructor currently requires a path. Review wants the no-argument case to keep logging without opening a file.
If no file is provided to the Logger constructor, where should log lines go by default?
Logging supports file and stdout output; stdout is the default.
If no file is provided to the Logger constructor, where should log lines go by default?
The scraper currently prints raw HTML. Emit a markdown table with two columns, Date and Holiday Name, escaping pipes in names.
In the holiday scraper output, print a markdown table header Date | Holiday Name, a delimiter row, then one data row per holiday.
The scraper Makefile will link libxml2. Before I apt-get anything I need the team's usual commands to see whether it is already present on Ubuntu.
How can I check if libxml2 is already installed in Ubuntu?
Library availability is verified with `dpkg -l` or `pkg-config`, and installation steps are documented.
How can I check if libxml2 is already installed in Ubuntu?
Log lines still print the full source path and concurrent tests interleave. I need the team's logger construction steps, including levels, serialized writes, and RAII streams.
Walk through how this repo builds a Logger that keeps only filename+extension, serializes concurrent writes, and owns its streams.

Design stdout-default with optional file, add levels, serialize concurrent writes, capture __FILE__/__LINE__ then keep filename+extension, own streams with RAII, compile a probe for both destinations.
Walk through how this repo builds a Logger that keeps only filename+extension, serializes concurrent writes, and owns its streams.
I need more than the library names. The holiday scrape still has to fetch HTML, select nodes, extract fields, and survive network errors.
What steps should the C++ holiday scraper follow from fetch through parse, extract, and error handling?
Fetch the URL with libcurl, parse HTML with libxml2 and XPath, extract fields, format output, handle network and parse errors without crashing, then link both libraries in the Makefile.
What steps should the C++ holiday scraper follow from fetch through parse, extract, and error handling?
The Makefile already has -lcurl. The HTML parse still fails at link time and I do not know whether a second library is required.
Besides libcurl, does this project's HTML scrape also need libxml2 on the link line?
Web scraping uses libcurl for HTTP and libxml2 for HTML parsing; both libraries must be checked and linked.
Besides libcurl, does this project's HTML scrape also need libxml2 on the link line?
Logs already print filename and line. I still cannot see which function emitted the line, and I need the project's diagnostic-macro set.
Is there a macro similar to __FILE__ and __LINE__ to output the function where the log was thrown?
__FILE__ provides a source path, __LINE__ a line number, and __func__ the function name; std::filesystem::path(__FILE__).filename() extracts only the filename.
Is there a macro similar to __FILE__ and __LINE__ to output the function where the log was thrown?
pkg-config says libxml2 exists, but the challenge still fails to compile. I need the rest of the team's verify-headers, document-install, probe, and rebuild sequence.
After pkg-config reports the library, what remaining checks does this repo run before trusting the link?
Verify development headers and linker flags, document apt-get for the -dev package if missing, compile a probe that includes the header and links the library, then rebuild the original target.

A log line dumped /home/me/day12/main.cpp:40. I need the project's way to keep only the filename from __FILE__.
How should __FILE__ be turned into just the filename in this C++ logger?
__FILE__ provides a source path; std::filesystem::path(__FILE__).filename() extracts only the filename.

Replace a raw FILE* in the logger with std::fstream so the file closes when the Logger is destroyed.
Open the log file with std::ofstream in the Logger constructor and let the destructor close it. Do not call fclose on a raw FILE*.
The Logger still fopen/fclose a FILE*. Switch the file destination to std::ofstream so it closes in the destructor.
If libcurl fails to fetch officeholidays.com, log the curl error and return a non-zero exit instead of parsing an empty body.
Write a Catch2 or GoogleTest case that constructs Logger with no path and asserts a line reaches stdout.
Write a Makefile in the holiday-scraper directory that compiles main.cpp and links -lcurl -lxml2.
When parsing the holiday HTML, free the libxml2 doc in all paths so a large page does not leak xmlDoc objects.

The Logger only prints one undifferentiated line format. I need INFO, WARN, and ERROR plus serialized writes so tests running in parallel do not interleave, and a probe that hits both stdout and an optional file.
Two threads log at once and the lines mix. Follow the team's logger construction so writes are serialized and streams stay RAII-owned.
Parse country and year out of an officeholidays.com URL of the form /country/year and pass them to the scraper.
Prefix each log line with a local timestamp using std::chrono and put_time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
Add YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS at the start of each Logger line using std::chrono::system_clock and std::put_time.
Holiday names contain UTF-8. After libcurl returns the body, keep the bytes as UTF-8 when feeding libxml2; do not recode as Latin-1.
Pass the libcurl response body to libxml2 without converting UTF-8 holiday names to Latin-1.
The Logger owns its ofstream exclusively. Use std::unique_ptr, not shared_ptr, for that member.
Store the optional log file as std::unique_ptr<std::ofstream> on the Logger. Do not use shared_ptr.
Run the Logger tests under AddressSanitizer or Valgrind and fix any leaks in the file-destination path.
Add Catch2 cases that feed the scraper a fixture HTML file and assert Date and Holiday Name rows.
